archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A pocket-bound starter who seldom scrambles, and whose value so far comes almost entirely from attacking 10-plus yards downfield rather than from his legs or the quick game.

report.headline: Remade accuracy and a downfield punch, but only 49 attempts of proof
report.take:
McCarthy arrives in this season as a reclamation project. His 2025 in Minnesota was rough: a -5.7 CPOE (56th of 63), a 21% bad-throw rate (57th) and 12 interceptions in 10 games, the profile of a young passer whose arm outran his accuracy. Now with the Giants, he spent the first weeks behind Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston. He played 6% of snaps in Week 5, took over for 40% in Week 6, and started Week 7 at Houston, a 27-21 overtime win in which he went 20/28 for 252.

The early version looks like a different thrower. His CPOE is 6.87 (4th of 45), his bad-throw rate is 6.1% (best among 38 charted qualifiers), and his 10.1 yards per attempt leads the position. The engine is depth. On throws of 10-plus air yards he is at 1.224 EPA per attempt with a 19.1 CPOE, and his 10 deep shots carry a 22.3 CPOE. Under 10 yards he is at -0.3 per play. All of his positive passing value has come downfield, and the short game has given some back. His time to throw is also down from last year's 3.02 to 2.85, a hint that he is getting the ball out with more decision than a year ago.

The numbers hide how little there is. Forty-nine attempts across one start and a half-game of relief can't settle whether the accuracy jump is real; a 12.6-point CPOE swing is the kind of change that needs a cause. A better supporting cast and a new staff are plausible causes, but the sample can't confirm them. The weak spots are just as thin but worth flagging. He is 22.2% on third-down conversions, facing an average of 9.3 yards to go, and has completed 1 of 5 red-zone throws. That sits behind a 2% TD rate (41st). He has also taken sacks at a 7.5% clip while being charted as pressured on just 4% of dropbacks.

The frame going forward is volume. John Harbaugh's offense passes 8.4 points less often than situation predicts (29th), so McCarthy's output will come from efficiency on 25-30 throws, not from piling up attempts. If the intermediate and deep accuracy holds even partway, he is a solid, efficiency-driven starter. If it slides back toward his 2025 baseline, the low volume leaves him little cushion.

strengths.title: Downfield accuracy and explosive value
strengths.body: His throws of 10-plus air yards have produced 1.224 EPA per attempt with a 19.1 CPOE, and he leads qualifiers in yards per attempt. That comes from hitting intermediate and deep windows on time, especially to Malik Nabers. Expect it to cool on more attempts, but this is the core of what makes him viable.

strengths.title: Ball placement transformed from 2025
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate has fallen from 21% to 6.1%, and his CPOE has swung 12.6 points. That is the single biggest question mark from his Vikings tape answered, at least for now. A tighter, quicker release (time to throw down 0.17 seconds) is one mechanical explanation. Half of it holding would still be a real improvement.

strengths.title: Nabers as a reliable first read
strengths.body: Nabers has drawn 15 of his targets at 0.572 EPA per target, giving McCarthy a go-to option who wins at the intermediate level where he is strongest. That connection is role-driven and should stay steady.

concerns.title: Short game giving value back
concerns.body: Under 10 air yards he sits at -0.3 EPA per play with a negative CPOE, and his one interception came there. Screens and checkdowns are low-value by design, but a -6.8 CPOE on short throws is a timing problem, not a scheme one. It is on 15 attempts, so treat it as a watch item.

concerns.title: Third down and red zone stalls
concerns.body: He has converted 22.2% of third downs and completed 20% in the red zone, which is why he has one TD despite elite per-attempt yardage. Long third downs (9.3 to go on average) explain part of it, and five red-zone plays is noise. The TD rate should climb, but scoring is the open question.

concerns.title: Sacks outpacing pressure
concerns.body: He took three sacks in his lone start (9.7% as a starter) despite a tiny charted pressure rate, and half his pressures became sacks. That points to holding the ball against coverage while waiting for the downfield shot, which is the cost of his vertical style. It merits watching as defenses get tape on him.

trend.note: His role went from 6% of snaps to 40% to 92% over three weeks, and his efficiency held from relief duty (5.0 EPA) into the start (5.6). The trend is real in role, while the efficiency is still unproven.

nextGame.headline: A pass-rush-free, leaky Eagles defense suits his downfield profile
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's defense ranks 27th in EPA allowed per dropback and dead last in both sack rate and hit rate. That is the ideal opponent for a passer who wants time to work the intermediate and deep levels, and it eases the sack worry above. The Eagles have also let WR1s score well above their usual output (29th), which sets up the Nabers connection. Their deep-ball defense is middling (14th), so the shots should be there without being free. Philadelphia's own offense ranks 29th in EPA, so the Giants may control the game and lean on the run, which caps his volume. No line or total is posted yet.

On the Eagles' side, edge rusher Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion) and cornerbacks Michael Carter II and Jakorian Bennett were all inactive. Each carries an estimated return before this game, so their availability is unsettled, but a missing Smith thins an already toothless rush. Lane Johnson, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks being out weakens Philadelphia's offense, which strengthens a controlled-script read. For the Giants, both Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. are questionable with hamstrings. If Skattebo misses, a run-first offense may lean more on McCarthy's arm. Theo Johnson's absence leaves Isaiah Likely as the tight end. The Giants also come off a bye, giving McCarthy two weeks of first-team preparation.

keyMatchups.title: No rush versus held-ball sacks
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia's league-worst sack rate meets McCarthy's tendency to take sacks while waiting downfield. If he stays clean here, his sack issue reads as a sample quirk; if he doesn't, it's a habit.

keyMatchups.title: Nabers against a soft WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia allows 0.54 EPA per play to top receivers (28th), and Nabers is McCarthy's most productive target. It is an early-season split that may reflect who the Eagles have faced, but it fits his profile.

keyMatchups.title: Run-heavy script capping attempts
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia's run defense ranks 31st and its offense 29th, which invites Harbaugh's already run-leaning offense to grind. That is good for winning but trims McCarthy's attempts.

nextGame.watch: Whether his 10-plus-yard accuracy holds on a full starter's workload with a clean pocket — the clearest test yet of whether the 2026 version is real.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a low-volume, efficiency-dependent starter. Harbaugh's offense won't push him much past 25-30 attempts, so a range of roughly 195-255 passing yards a game is realistic. His yards per attempt should drift down from 10.1 toward the high 7s or low 8s as the sample grows. His TD rate is the most likely thing to rise, since a 2% rate with an offense ranked mid-pack is more bad luck in five red-zone plays than skill. Plan on 1 to 1.6 touchdowns a game. His rushing will be a minor factor: one scramble all year, and designed runs have gone nowhere.

The sustainability question is the accuracy. A CPOE near the top of the league from a passer who sat 56th a year ago will regress some. The issue is whether it settles around average, which still supports this offense, or slides back toward 2025's level, when interceptions piled up. His interception rate is about league average now, and that is the stat to watch for early signs of slippage.
swingFactors: Whether the downfield accuracy holds on starter volume
Skattebo's hamstring and the Giants' run-pass balance
Red-zone finishing turning yards into touchdowns

confidence.note: 49 attempts, one start, and a sharp break from his 2025 profile.
